targets.name: gguf-lfm25-12b-unsloth
targets.notes: TIER A: architectural outlier (hybrid conv/attention) exercising different llama.cpp quantization kernels. 3.07 GB. LiquidAI LFM Open License ('other') — read before redistributing completions.

targets.name: gguf-llama32-3b-bartowski
targets.notes: TIER B: one of the most-deployed local-inference artifacts (172,650 30d downloads). 8.45 GB pair. Llama 3.2 Community License; GGUF repo ungated.

targets.name: gguf-phi4-mini-unsloth
targets.notes: TIER B: phi family; conservative refusal tuning makes it a good place to look for quantization-induced refusal REMOVAL. 10.17 GB. MIT, ungated.

targets.name: gguf-smollm3-3b-bartowski
targets.notes: TIER B: fully-open base (weights+data+recipe) — a flip here is the most reproducible finding in the set. 8.07 GB. apache-2.0, ungated.

targets.name: gguf-ministral-8b-bartowski
targets.notes: TIER C, prune candidate (20.96 GB pair, 7,880 30d downloads): the mistral-family slot — clean text-only MistralForCausalLM base, f16 16.05 GB just under the 16.5 GB cap. Mistral Research License ('other') — read before redistributing completions.

targets.name: gguf-gemma2-2b-it-bartowski
targets.notes: TIER C, prune candidate (12.17 GB; the only unquantized file is f32): deployment-dominant gemma artifact, 178,165 30d downloads (3rd among GGUF rows). Gemma Terms of Use govern redistribution of derived outputs.

targets.name: gguf-olmo2-7b-bartowski
targets.notes: TIER C, prune second (19.07 GB, 14,724 30d downloads): the only fully-open-everything 7B in the set (AI2). apache-2.0, ungated.

targets.name: gguf-qwen3-8b-unsloth
targets.notes: TIER C, prune first (21.42 GB, the largest line item) BUT the highest-download both-arm repo on the list (318,290 30d) and the only 8B-class entry (8.19B params — at the cap's edge; the binding cap is the 16.5 GB baseline file, which the 16.39 GB BF16 clears). apache-2.0, ungated, fully redistributable.

targets.name: ct-qwen25-15b-anchor-crusadersk
targets.notes: REQUIRED ANCHOR with a DISCLOSURE: this is the maintainer's own self-produced quant (known prior finding: 2/10 over-refusal), NOT a third-party artifact. The compressed-tensors prevalence bound must be quoted both with and without this row. compressed-tensors format (despite 'awq' in the name), W4A16_ASYM g128. apache-2.0.

targets.name: ct-qwen25-15b-official-awq
targets.notes: Controlled comparison against the anchor: same baseline weights, DIFFERENT scheme (real autoawq gemm 4-bit g128, first-party, 835,675 30d downloads). Loads via transformers' AwqQuantizer, which requires gptqmodel — pip install 'quantfit[awq]'. Stratum covers transformers-loadable quants; the bound's autoawq membership is disclosed in the curation file. apache-2.0. UNRUNNABLE ON WINDOWS, measured 2026-08-21: transformers' AwqQuantizer routes through gptqmodel, whose AWQ kernel validation imports triton, and triton does not ship for Windows. Fails with ModuleNotFoundError regardless of disk or VRAM, so it is not a capacity problem and re-running on a bigger box will not help - it needs a Linux host. It is kept in the manifest deliberately: `screen` records it as an error row, and a target silently removed would overstate coverage of the compressed-tensors stratum, which is only 3 targets wide. Evidence: validation/2026-08-21-screen-complete/.

targets.name: ct-granite31-2b-redhat-w4a16
targets.notes: Breaks the CT stratum out of qwen-only: IBM Granite family, RedHatAI producer (the reference llm-compressor publisher). W4A16 g64 symmetric, 6.77 GB, 34,159 30d downloads. apache-2.0, ungated.
